rationale: The student struggles with one-to-one correspondence, double-counting and skipping objects. Placing counters onto a structured ten-frame reinforces placing exactly one counter per slot and per number word, establishing a physical tracking constraint.
intent: Target one-to-one counting discipline within 1 to 7 using concrete counter placement on a single ten-frame; avoid using 8 objects so as not to duplicate the student's current task.

data.title: Counting Objects to 7
data.description: Place counters one by one on the ten-frame to practice one-to-one counting up to 7.

challenges.hint: Place two red counters on the frame one at a time.
challenges.narration: Let's start by placing two counters on our ten-frame.
challenges.instruction: Put 2 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Count carefully as you place three counters on the frame.
challenges.narration: Now, let's put three counters on the frame.
challenges.instruction: Put 3 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill the top row as you count up to four.
challenges.narration: Can you place four counters on the frame?
challenges.instruction: Put 4 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill the entire top row of the ten-frame.
challenges.narration: Let's fill the entire top row by placing five counters.
challenges.instruction: Put 5 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Put five on top, and one more on the bottom row.
challenges.narration: Great job! Now let's build the number six.
challenges.instruction: Put 6 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Place five on the top row and two on the bottom row.
challenges.narration: Let's make seven counters on the frame.
challenges.instruction: Put 7 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Check your count to make sure you have exactly seven counters.
challenges.narration: Let's practice our final challenge and build seven counters again.
challenges.instruction: Put 7 counters on the ten frame!

judgement.reasoning: The student struggles with one-to-one correspondence and keeping track of counted items in a scattered or unorganized set (counting 8 as 10). Placing counters one-by-one into distinct cells of a ten-frame directly constrains the spatial organization (one item per box), preventing double-counting or skipping. The progression starts low (2, 3) and scaffolds up to 7 without repeating 8.
judgement.verdict: Yes, using structured placement on a ten-frame provides the exact spatial grounding needed to fix skipping and double-counting.
